title: Explicit results on the distribution of zeros of Hecke $L$-functions
publication_status: published journal article; pinned arXiv PDF is the proof source
audit_scope: Theorem 1.1 and definitions checked in v1. Journal identity has a different title.
statement: Theorem 1.1 gives the effective log-free bound \(\sum_{\chi(H)=1}N(\sigma,T,\chi)\ll\{e^{O(n_K)}D_K^2QT^{n_K}\}^{81(1-\sigma)}\) for \(1/2\le\sigma<1\) and \(T\ge\max\{n_K D_K^{-2/n_K}Q^{-3/(5n_K)},1\}\). Here \(H\bmod\mathfrak q\) is a congruence class group in a number field \(K\) and \(Q\) is the largest primitive conductor norm for characters trivial on \(H\). The exponent constant 74 applies for \(1-10^{-3}\le\sigma<1\).

title: An explicit bound for the least prime ideal in the Chebotarev density theorem
publication_status: published journal article; pinned arXiv PDF is the proof source
audit_scope: Density theorem and main Chebotarev setup inspected, proofs outside scope.
statement: Theorem 3.2 gives \(\sum_{\chi\bmod H}N(\sigma,T,\chi)\ll\{e^{O(n_K)}D_K^2QT^{n_K+2}\}^{81(1-\sigma)}\) for \(1/2\le\sigma<1\), \(T\ge\max\{n_K^{5/6}D_K^{-4/(3n_K)}Q^{-4/(9n_K)},1\}\), with 73.5 replacing 81 for \(1-10^{-3}\le\sigma<1\). The Chebotarev application uses this family density theorem with the separate repulsion estimate and an abelian subgroup meeting the target conjugacy class.

title: More than five-twelfths of the zeros of $\zeta$ are on the critical line
publication_status: published journal article; pinned arXiv PDF is the proof source
audit_scope: Theorem 1.2, surrounding optimization and statement of the mollified main moment checked. Long proofs outside scope.
statement: Theorem 1.2 proves more than \(5/12\) of zeta zeros are on the critical line. The numerical optimization in the introduction gives \(\kappa>0.417293\) and \(\kappa^*\ge0.407511\) for the simple critical proportion. These are different counts, both based on mollified twisted second moments.

title: An unconditional $\mathrm{GL}(n)$ large sieve
publication_status: published journal article; pinned arXiv PDF is the proof source
audit_scope: Theorems 1.1–1.2 and family definition checked in v6.
statement: Theorem 1.2 bounds the sum of \(N_\pi(\sigma,T)=\#\{\rho:\beta>\sigma,\,|\gamma|\le T\}\) over cuspidal \(\pi\) on \(\mathrm{GL}_n\) over \(F\) of analytic conductor at most \(Q\) by \(O_{n,[F:\mathbb Q]}((QT^{[F:\mathbb Q]})^{(7/10)n^4(1-\sigma)})\), for \(Q,T\ge1\), \(0\le\sigma\le1\). The log-free estimate is unconditional in this family and does not assume Ramanujan.

title: A zero density estimate for Dedekind zeta functions
publication_status: published journal article; pinned arXiv PDF is the proof source
audit_scope: Theorems 1.1 and 2.1 and quotient count checked. Journal issue date differs from online first.
statement: For a finite nontrivial group \(G\) and a family \(\mathcal F_G(Q)\) of Galois \(K/\mathbb Q\) with group \(G\) and discriminant at most \(Q\), Theorem 1.1 sums the zero counts for \(\zeta_K/\zeta\). For \(\sigma\ge0,\ Q,T\ge2\), the result is \(O_{|G|}(m_{\mathcal F_G}(Q)(QT)^{(7/10)|G|^3(1-\sigma)}(\log QT)^{|G|^2})\), with \(m\) the maximal number of family fields intersecting one chosen member nontrivially.

title: Explicit zero density estimate for the Riemann zeta-function near the critical line
venue: Journal of Mathematical Analysis and Applications
publication_status: published journal article; pinned arXiv PDF is the proof source
audit_scope: Theorem 1 and definition of H0 checked in v2. Numerical estimates and journal proof comparison outside read scope.
statement: For the verification height \(H_0=3.0610046\times10^{10}\) used by the paper, Theorem 1 proves \(N(\sigma,2T)-N(\sigma,T)\le10395.2\,T^{1-(\sigma-1/2)/4}\log T+1.104\log^2T+0.173\log T\log\log T+0.51\log T\) for \(T\ge H_0,\ 1/2\le\sigma\le0.831\). The interval is dyadic rather than of sublinear length.

title: Explicit zero density for the Riemann zeta function
venue: Journal of Mathematical Analysis and Applications
publication_status: published journal article; pinned arXiv PDF is the proof source
audit_scope: Theorem and explicit constant locators checked in arXiv copy.
statement: Theorem 1.1, (1.7), gives \(N(\sigma,T)\le(C_1/(2\pi d))T^{8(1-\sigma)/3}(\log(kT))^{2\sigma}(\log T)^{5-4\sigma}+(C_2/(2\pi d))(\log T)^2\) for \(T\ge H_0,\ \sigma>1/2+d/\log H_0\), with \(10^9/H_0\le k\le1,\ H\in[1002,H_0),\ \alpha>0,\delta\ge1,\ 1+\eta_0\le\mu\le1+\eta,\ \eta\in(\eta_0,1/2)\), \(d>0\), and \(\eta_0=0.23622\ldots\). The preceding displayed (1.6) retains the logarithm with smaller numerical value. Constants \(C_1,C_2\) are explicit in (4.72)–(4.73).
version_note: The 2018 journal article predates the 2021 arXiv deposit.

title: Half-isolated zeros and zero-density estimates
publication_status: published journal article; pinned arXiv PDF is the proof source
audit_scope: Hypothesis F, Theorem 1 and the beginning of the detector statements checked in v2. Full proof outside scope.
statement: Under Hypothesis F that all nontrivial zeta zeros lie on finitely many fixed vertical lines, Theorem 1 gives \(N(\sigma,T)\ll T^{2(1-\sigma)}\exp((\log\log T)^{O(1)})\). Half-isolated zeros admit short detecting polynomials, and the argument separates horizontal and vertical clustering. The hypothesis is weaker than RH but remains an extra restriction on zeta zeros.

title: An explicit Vinogradov-Korobov zero-free region for Dirichlet L-functions
publication_status: published journal article; pinned arXiv PDF is the proof source
audit_scope: Theorem 1.1 and the height/conductor parameter definitions checked in v1.
statement: For every character modulo \(q\ge3\), Theorem 1.1 excludes zeros for \(|t|\ge10\) and \(\sigma\ge1-[10.5\log q+61.5(\log|t|)^{2/3}(\log\log|t|)^{1/3}]^{-1}\). Beyond an absolute effectively computable threshold it replaces \(10.5,61.5\) by \(10.1,49.13\). This high-height result does not rule out a possible low real exceptional zero.

title: Explicit zero-free regions for the Riemann zeta-function
publication_status: published journal article; pinned arXiv PDF is the proof source
audit_scope: Theorems 1.1–1.3 checked in v1. Polynomial numerical verification outside scope.
statement: Theorems 1.1–1.2 exclude zeros for \(\sigma\ge1-[C(\log|t|)^{2/3}(\log\log|t|)^{1/3}]^{-1}\) with \(C=55.241\) for \(|t|\ge3\), and \(C=48.1588\) for sufficiently large \(|t|\). Theorem 1.3 excludes zeros for \(\sigma\ge1-(5.558691\log|t|)^{-1}\) and \(|t|\ge2\). These are distinct height-dependent regions.

title: Explicit bounds on $\zeta(s)$ in the critical strip and a zero-free region
venue: Journal of Mathematical Analysis and Applications
publication_status: published journal article; pinned arXiv PDF is the proof source
audit_scope: Theorem 1.1 and Corollary 1.2 checked in v2. No independent verification of the numerical optimization or comparison to subsequent bounds.
statement: Theorem 1.1 gives \(|\zeta(\sigma_k+it)|\le1.546\,t^{1/(2^k-2)}\log t\) for \(k\ge4,\ \sigma_k=1-k/(2^k-2),\ t\ge3\). Corollary 1.2 excludes zeros for \(|t|\ge3,\ \sigma>1-\log\log|t|/(21.233\log|t|)\), an explicit Littlewood-type region used in later finite-height patching.

title: Explicit bounds for the Riemann zeta function and a new zero-free region
venue: Journal of Mathematical Analysis and Applications
publication_status: published journal article; pinned arXiv PDF is the proof source
audit_scope: Theorem 1.1, v1 numbers in Theorem 1.2, and asymptotic distinction checked.
statement: Theorem 1.1 bounds \(|\zeta(\sigma+it)|\) and \(|\zeta(\sigma+it,u)-u^{-(\sigma+it)}|\) by \(70.6995\,|t|^{4.43795(1-\sigma)^{3/2}}(\log|t|)^{2/3}\), for \(|t|\ge3,\ 1/2\le\sigma\le1,\ 0<u\le1\) in the Hurwitz case. Theorem 1.2 gives a Vinogradov–Korobov denominator 54.004 for \(|t|\ge3\) in this v1, and the subsequent sufficiently-large-height constant is 48.0718.
version_note: The March 2026 Bellotti–Trudgian–Yang preprint cites the journal work with 53.989 instead of v1’s 54.004. That is evidence of a version difference, not a comparison of the journal proof itself.

title: A remark on density theorems for Riemann's zeta-function
publication_status: published journal article; pinned arXiv PDF is the proof source
audit_scope: Full read pp. 1–14, including detector, Halász estimate, Theorem 2 and references. Theorem 1 range visually checked against (3.1).
statement: Writing \(N(1-\eta,T)\ll_\epsilon T^{\eta B(\eta)+\epsilon}\), the detector proof gives \(B(\eta)\le\max(4u_\ell,3v_\ell)\) on \(0<\eta<\min(1/3,2^{-\ell})\), with \(u_\ell=\mu(1-2^{-\ell})/(2^{-\ell}-\eta)\), \(v_\ell=\mu(1-2^{-(\ell-1)})/[2(2^{-\ell}-\eta)]\). Corollary 4 gives \(B(\eta)\le1/(1-4\eta)\) for \(0<\eta<1/4\); Corollary 1 conditionally gives \(N(\sigma,T)\ll_{\sigma,\epsilon}T^\epsilon\) for fixed \(\sigma>3/4\) under Lindelöf.
version_note: Theorem 1 on v1 p. 5 prints max rather than min in its range, inconsistent with the proof and with denominators that vanish in the extra interval. The journal text was not independently compared.

title: A note on the zeros of $L$-functions associated to fixed-order Dirichlet characters
venue: Bulletin of the Australian Mathematical Society
publication_status: published journal article; pinned arXiv PDF is the proof source
audit_scope: Main table of Theorems 2.1–2.3 and family definition checked in v2.
statement: For \(Q,T\ge2,\ 1/2<\sigma<1\), Theorem 2.1 sums zero counts over primitive quadratic characters of conductor at most \(Q\), giving \(O_\epsilon((QT)^\epsilon\min\{(QT)^{8(1-\sigma)/3},(Q^8T^5)^{(1-\sigma)/(6\sigma-3)}\})\). Theorems 2.2–2.3 handle orders 3, 6 and 4 with their own conductor exponents.

title: Explicit zero density estimate near unity
publication_status: arXiv preprint; journal status unverified
audit_scope: Theorems 1.1–1.3 checked. Author publications page states results are incorporated into the PhD thesis; no separate journal DOI verified.
statement: Theorem 1.2 gives \(N(\sigma,T)\le C_1^\prime T^{57.8875(1-\sigma)^{3/2}}(\log T)^{10393/900}\) uniformly for \(\sigma\in[0.98,1]\), \(T\ge3\), with \(C_1^\prime\) tabulated by height. Theorem 1.3 gives \(C_1^\prime=4.45\times10^{12}\) for \(T\ge\exp(6.7\times10^{12})\) in the same real-part range. The power of \(\log T\) is part of the bound.

title: An explicit log-free zero density estimate for the Riemann zeta-function
publication_status: published journal article; pinned arXiv PDF is the proof source
audit_scope: Theorem 1.1, its one-constant specialization and Table 2 provenance checked in v2.
statement: Theorem 1.1 gives \(N(\sigma,T)\le C T^{B(1-\sigma)}\) with height and real-part parameters specified in Table 2. A single explicit instance has \(B=1.448,\ C=1.62\times10^{11}\), \(3\times10^{12}<T\le\exp(6.7\times10^{12})\) and \(0.9927\le\sigma\le1\). The finite upper height is essential for interpreting this log-free estimate.

title: An explicit form of Ingham's zero density estimate
publication_status: arXiv preprint; journal status unverified
audit_scope: Corollary 1 and the uniformity/uses of the intervals checked in v2. See the October Ouimet dependency audit for a specific use of the resulting uniform Ingham exponent. Contents of v1 not treated as interchangeable.
statement: For \(T\ge H_{\rm RH}\), Corollary 1 gives \(N(\sigma,T)\le B_1T^{3(1-\sigma)/(2-\sigma)}(\log T)^{(7-5\sigma)/(2-\sigma)}+B_2\log^2T+B_3\log T\). The constants apply on the 16 subintervals \([n/32,(n+1)/32]\), \(16\le n\le31\), of Table 1. The strength for moving near-line \(\sigma\) is uniform in each fixed table interval, with explicit logs and the Ingham power intact.

title: Zero-free regions inspired by work of Heath-Brown
publication_status: arXiv preprint; journal status unverified
audit_scope: Read opening theorem statements, patch ranges and ending of the proof of Lemma 1. Numerical optimization and positivity proof not fully audited.
statement: Theorem 1 excludes zeta zeros for \(t\ge3,\ \sigma>1-(4.896\log t)^{-1}\), followed by conjugation for negative heights. Its finite argument through \(\exp(76.47)\) and the explicit Littlewood region beyond \(\exp(76.463)\) overlap. The preprint also displays a 4.8594 variant whose text makes the conclusion depend on the thesis bound and on a stronger finite Lemma 2 through \(\exp(56.693)\).
version_note: In v1 p. 3 the stronger variant is phrased as following once Lemma 2 is established. The proof ending explicitly concludes Lemma 1 only. Kept the 4.8594 entry as a displayed but unclosed variant in this source scope.

title: Large zeta sums and zeros of the Riemann zeta function
publication_status: arXiv preprint; journal status unverified
audit_scope: Full 19-page reading, including pretentious twist, Hadamard comparison, Gaussian pole, detection, exponent-pair range and references.
statement: For \(T\le|t|\le2T,\ \exp(\sqrt{\log T})\le x\le\sqrt T\), a value \(|\sum_{n\le x}n^{it}|=x/N\) with \(1\le N\le(\log x)^{1/100}\) forces a common \(\phi\) with \(|\phi-t|\le cN\). For every \(cN^6\le L\le(\log x)/2\), its open disk about \(1+i\phi\) of radius \(L\log T/(\log x)^2\) has at least \(L/360\) zero copies. Theorem 1.2 runs in the reverse direction as a sufficient local zero count condition for a logarithmic saving in the arithmetic sum.

title: More than 83.69% of the zeros of the Riemann zeta function are distinct
publication_status: arXiv preprint; journal status unverified
audit_scope: v2 Theorem 1 and scope of formal portions read. Primary source claim only for the new numerical bound and its numerical dependency.
statement: Theorem 1 of v2 claims \(\liminf N_d(T)/N(T)\ge 16260119298029/19426831050000=0.83699288145242\ldots\), for distinct nontrivial zeros versus total multiplicity. The clipping argument is stated to be partly Lean-checked and the constant imports a computer-assisted local inequality from a non-refereed work. Neither external inequality nor a whole-theorem kernel replay is established by this record.
version_note: The unchanged title rounds the result more conservatively than the v2 theorem. The v2 abstract explicitly identifies the external numerical dependency.

title: More than 8/9 zeros of the Riemann zeta function are simple or on the critical line
publication_status: arXiv preprint; journal status unverified
audit_scope: v1 definitions, Theorem 1 and numerical constant locator checked. The long analytic/numerical chain was not independently validated.
statement: Theorem 1 claims \(\liminf N_{s\cup0}(T)/N(T)>8/9\), with \(N_{s\cup0}=N_s+N_0-N_{0s}\). This is a union, so a multiple critical zero contributes its multiplicity; the excluded copies are exactly the multiple off-axis zeros. It is distinct from a lower bound on the intersection of simple and critical zeros. The paper reports approximately \(0.88893\) for its optimized constant.

title: Isolated zeros of the Riemann zeta function and zeros of linear combinations of Dirichlet $L$-functions
publication_status: arXiv preprint; journal status unverified
audit_scope: v2 Theorems 1.1, 1.3 and 1.5 and the ordered multiplicity convention checked. Formula uses log T precisely as displayed; the introductory local-spacing convention uses log ordinate.
statement: Theorem 1.1 claims \(\liminf B_0(T,c)/N(T)\ge0.6552\ldots\) for some fixed \(c>0\) and \(\ge0.50875\) for \(c=1/6\), where \(B_0\) requires each adjacent ordered-ordinate gap to exceed \(2\pi c/\log T\) at a zero with \(0<\gamma\le T\). For a distinct pair of primitive characters of the same conductor and parity, Theorem 1.5 claims at least 31% odd-multiplicity critical zeros for linear combinations with nonzero real coefficients and the source’s respective root-number phase factors.
version_note: v2 arXiv history records corrected typos and expanded introduction/exposition.
